facts.text: Systems and software engineering standards provide general practices for organizing a system's life cycle, documenting tests, describing architecture, writing assurance cases, performing verification and validation, and managing risk.
facts.quote: These are the general standards for how to run an engineering project: how to organize a system's life cycle, document tests, describe an architecture, write an assurance case, verify and validate, and manage risk.

facts.text: The listed systems and software engineering standards do not mention collisions or brakes; the booklet cites them as documented practice supporting a safety program.
facts.quote: None of these mentions a collision or a brake; they are the scaffolding a safety program is built on, and the booklet cites them as documented practice.

facts.text: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 defines system life-cycle processes and, together with handbooks from the International Council on Systems Engineering (INCOSE) and NASA, forms the backbone of verification and validation planning.
facts.quote: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 defines system life-cycle processes and, with the handbooks of the International Council on Systems Engineering (INCOSE) and NASA, is the backbone of verification and validation planning

facts.text: IEEE 1012-2016 is the standard for system, software and hardware verification and validation.
facts.quote: IEEE 1012-2016 is the standard for system, software and hardware verification and validation [Chapter 12].

facts.text: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3:2021 defines test documentation, including plan, design, case and completion reports.
facts.quote: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3:2021 defines test documentation (plan, design, case and completion reports)

facts.text: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3:2021 and Part 4:2021 have no collision-avoidance content, but supply discipline for separating test processes, techniques and documentation.
facts.quote: they have "no collision-avoidance content" but supply the discipline of separating test processes, techniques and documentation [Chapter 9].

facts.text: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 covers architecture description using several views matched to the viewer's role rather than one universal diagram.
facts.quote: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 covers architecture description, the idea of several views matched to the viewer's role rather than one universal diagram

facts.text: The booklet applies ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 to the simulation toolchain by marking which elements are real, modeled, emulated or substituted.
facts.quote: the booklet applies it to the simulation toolchain, marking which elements are real, modeled, emulated or substituted [Chapter 12].

facts.text: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2:2022 standardizes the assurance case as a structured argument from claims through evidence.
facts.quote: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2:2022 standardizes the assurance case, the structured argument from claims through evidence [Chapter 12].

facts.text: ISO 31000:2018 and IEC 31010:2019 document risk-management practice and risk-assessment techniques that form the basis of the risk register.
facts.quote: ISO 31000:2018 and IEC 31010:2019 document risk-management practice and risk-assessment techniques, the basis of the risk register

facts.text: The booklet notes that outcome evidence for risk registers is thin.
facts.quote: the booklet notes that outcome evidence for risk registers is thin [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The collision-mitigation validation program's final evidentiary question is whether a safety board can trust a virtual result enough to support a safety decision.
facts.quote: The program's final question is evidentiary: can a safety board trust a virtual result enough to support a safety decision?

facts.text: The systems and software engineering standards supply the structure for an evidence plan tracing each claim to its evidence, method, acceptance criterion, owner and gate; they do not specify what to test, but ensure that tested items are traceable.
facts.quote: These standards supply the structure for an evidence plan that traces each claim to its evidence, method, acceptance criterion, owner and gate [Chapter 12]. They do not say what to test; they make sure nothing tested is untraceable.
